passage:
Layla: Our council wants to organise a charity market next month, but we must agree on important details first.
Yousuf: What is the event's main purpose? I heard several clubs suggested different projects this year.
Layla: We chose an accessible reading corner. Younger pupils need large-print books and better lighting in the library.
Yousuf: Will students collect money, donate books, or offer their time to improve the reading space?
Layla: All three. The finance teacher will count donations with two witnesses and keep a written record.
Yousuf: Why two witnesses? Our volunteers have always been reliable when organising school activities.
Layla: Transparent records protect everyone from misunderstanding. That is good practice, not an accusation against volunteers.
Yousuf: Will families pay an entrance fee? That might discourage some people from joining the event.
Layla: Entry will be free, but our stall will sell homemade cards with prices displayed clearly.
Yousuf: What about damaged second-hand books? Some donations might be unsuitable for young readers.
Layla: Volunteers will check the books and send unsuitable items to an appropriate recycling collection.
Yousuf: Parents have offered to prepare food. How will customers know whether dishes contain allergens?
Layla: Our team will provide ingredient cards and ask families not to use nuts in any dishes.
Yousuf: Can younger children help at the stalls, or will only older pupils be involved?
Layla: Older students will manage payments with a teacher. Younger pupils can welcome visitors and arrange books.
Yousuf: When will the market open, and how much time will families have to visit?
Layla: On Saturday morning, from nine until noon, when the school building is available for community activities.
Yousuf: Last year's online notice named the wrong location. How will you avoid confusion this time?
Layla: We will publish confirmed details on the school website and beside the main gate.
Yousuf: Some visitors may not want their photographs shared online. Have you prepared a consent policy?
Layla: Yes. We will never publish a visitor's photograph without asking for clear permission first.
Yousuf: What happens if the donations fail to reach your target? Will families receive an update?
Layla: We will report the total collected and actual purchases, then plan another event if necessary.
Yousuf: Who will decide what equipment to buy? Attractive items are not always the most useful.
Layla: Pupils will test the reading corner and recommend the changes that help them most.
Yousuf: Can families share suggestions as well, or is the survey only for pupils?
Layla: There will be an anonymous feedback box, so nobody must write their name.
Yousuf: Then the market teaches integrity as well as raising money. I can help at the book stall.
